quizzes.title: Color Theory & Harmonic Schemes Quiz
quizzes.description: Assess your foundational understanding of primary, secondary, and complementary color harmonies, warm vs cool balance, and optical contrast.

questions.prompt: Which color scheme utilizes three hues that are evenly spaced around the 12-hue color wheel?
questions.explanation: A triadic color scheme forms an equilateral triangle on the color wheel (e.g. Red, Yellow, and Blue).

questions.prompt: When two complementary colors are placed directly adjacent at full saturation, what visual effect is produced?
questions.explanation: Complementary pairs create the highest possible chromatic tension and vivid contrast when juxtaposed.

questions.prompt: In traditional fine art pigment mixing, what is the term for a color produced by adding white to a pure hue?
questions.explanation: A tint is made by adding white. A shade is created by adding black, and a tone is created with neutral grey.

questions.prompt: In two-dimensional pictorial space, warm colors (reds, yellows, oranges) typically have what spatial tendency?
questions.explanation: Longer wavelength warm colors visually expand and advance, whereas shorter wavelength cool colors recede.

quizzes.title: Human Proportions & Volumetric Skeletal Form Quiz
quizzes.description: Test your grasp of classical 8-head proportional ratios, contrapposto balance axes, and thoracic foreshortening.

questions.prompt: In classical idealistic figure drawing, the adult human body is traditionally calibrated to how many head lengths tall?
questions.explanation: The standard classical academic canon measures an adult standing figure at approximately 7.5 to 8 heads tall.

questions.prompt: What happens to the pelvis and shoulder axes during a dynamic contrapposto stance?
options: They lock into a rigid 90-degree square
They align horizontally with the floor
questions.explanation: Contrapposto shifts weight to one leg, causing the pelvic tilt to oppose the shoulder tilt in an organic S-curve rhythm.

questions.prompt: When drawing a cylinder or limb projecting directly toward the viewer, which drafting technique is crucial to convey depth?
options: Overlapping volumetric ellipses and foreshortened contour wrapping
questions.explanation: Curved cross-contour wrapping lines and overlapping elliptical forms communicate cylindrical compression toward the viewer.

quizzes.title: Nuqta Metric System & Qalam Geometry Quiz
quizzes.description: Verify your knowledge of proportional script measurements, pen nib slicing angles, and classical Islamic calligraphy rules.

questions.prompt: In the proportioned script system (al-Khatt al-Mansub) formalized by Ibn Muqla, what is the foundational unit of measurement?
options: The Nuqta (rhomboid dot made by the pen nib)
questions.explanation: The Nuqta (rhombic dot created by pressing the cut reed nib flat on parchment) is the master unit calibrating all letter heights.

questions.prompt: In classical Thuluth script, the master letter Alif is conventionally calibrated to a height of how many Nuqtas?
questions.explanation: The majestic vertical stroke of the Alif in classical Thuluth is precisely 7 rhomboid Nuqta dots high.

questions.prompt: What angle is standard for trimming the nib of a traditional reed pen (Qalam) for Naskh or Thuluth script?
questions.explanation: A 35° to 45° angled oblique bevel gives the calligrapher simultaneous control over hairline connections and broad downstrokes.
